chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Suleyman ibn Muhammad al-Khash'ami, from Ishaq al-Taweel al-Attar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to spend on perfume more than what he used to spend on food.
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad spend more on food or perfume?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) emphasis on al-ṭīb (perfume) as a means of enhancing one’s appearance for social and spiritual occasions, reflecting the Shia tradition of valuing cleanliness and dignity. By prioritizing scent over mere sustenance, the Prophet illustrated that personal grooming is not merely aesthetic but a form of worship and respect for others, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic practice of using musk and oud for prayer and gatherings.
